name: What should I ask a contractor before starting an open-concept kitchen conversion?

mainEntity.name: What questions should I ask a contractor before hiring them for an open-concept kitchen conversion?
mainEntity.text: What questions should I ask a contractor before hiring them for an open-concept kitchen conversion?

acceptedAnswer.text: Before hiring a contractor, ask questions that reveal whether they understand open-concept conversions as a structural and design project, not just a demolition job. The contractor should explain how they identify load-bearing walls, whether they work with a structural engineer, who prepares permit drawings, and how inspections are scheduled. Ask how they handle flooring transitions, ceiling patching, lighting redesign, dust control, and temporary support during demolition. You should also ask what happens if hidden issues appear after walls are opened, because older homes often contain surprises. A strong contractor will give a clear process, a written scope, a realistic timeline, and line items for structural and finish work. If they only talk about demolition and cabinets, that is a warning sign. Open-concept projects need coordination, so the right team should be able to explain the order of work from design through final punch list.
acceptedAnswer.description: Ask whether they handle structural assessment, permit drawings, engineering coordination, inspections, flooring tie-ins, and electrical or plumbing changes. You should also ask how they protect the rest of the home, manage dust, and handle unexpected structural issues.
